title: Real-Time Correlation of Relaxation, Dephasing, and Two-level System Dynamics in Transmon Qubits
authors: Ambrose Yang, Alexander M. Young, Paal H. Prestegaard, Atharv Joshi, Matthew S. Ai, Q. Rumman Rahman, Faranak Bahrami, Matthew P. Bland, Jui-Lin Niu, Ourania-Maria Glezakou-Elbert, Ray D. Chang, Jocelyn Liu, Zhengyi Lu, Robert J. Cava, Nathalie P. de Leon, Andrew A. Houck
abstract: Materials improvements in transmon qubits have yielded remarkable advances in qubit lifetimes (T1)and coherence times (T2). However, state-of-the-art superconducting qubits experience temporal fluctuations in their performance, which limit gate fidelities and quantum processor performance. We observe correlated increases in qubit relaxation and dephasing rates that last for minutes to hours, which we call T1 and T2 excursions. Using interleaved lifetime and coherence time measurements, noise spectroscopy, and two-level-system (TLS) spectroscopy, we find that these excursions are caused by single or few strongly-coupled TLS defects that spectrally diffuse into resonance with the qubit frequency. Our measurement protocol provides a powerful tool for understanding the noise sources that cause temporal fluctuations in superconducting qubit performance.
summary: This research investigates performance degradation in superconducting transmon qubits caused by transient noise fluctuations. By combining interleaved measurements and TLS spectroscopy, the authors demonstrate that these performance dips are caused by individual, strongly-coupled defects (TLSs) resonating with the qubit frequency. This work establishes a powerful diagnostic tool for understanding and mitigating solid-state noise in quantum computing hardware.
main_problem: The paper addresses the temporal fluctuations (excursions) in qubit relaxation ($T_1$) and coherence ($T_2$) times in superconducting qubits, which degrade gate fidelity.
main_result: These performance excursions are strongly correlated with the spectral diffusion of individual, strongly-coupled Two-Level Systems (TLSs) that enter resonance with the qubit frequency.
method: The authors used interleaved lifetime/coherence measurements, noise spectroscopy (CPMG), and TLS spectroscopy to correlate noise sources with qubit decay rates.
model_or_system: The physical system is a Transmon qubit fabricated on a Ta-on-Si substrate. The noise is modeled by contributions from broadband losses and discrete, strongly-coupled TLS defects.
key_observables: Relaxation rate ($\Gamma_1$), dephasing rate ($\Gamma_\phi$), and the noise spectral density $S(\omega)$.
important_parameters: Excursion timescales (minutes to hours); TLS coupling strengths; correlation coefficients (e.g., $ho=0.51$ for $\Gamma_1$ vs $\Gamma_\phi$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the observed noise is dominated by TLS defects, which are modeled using Lorentzian spectral densities.
figures_summary: Figures show temporal traces of $T_1$ and gate fidelities exhibiting fluctuations, and scatter plots demonstrating the correlation between $\Gamma_1$ and $\Gamma_\phi$ during these excursions.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from observing the problem (fluctuating $T_1/T_2$) to developing a measurement protocol (interleaved measurements) and finally attributing the fluctuations to specific noise sources (TLS spectral diffusion).
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed experimental methodology for characterizing and diagnosing specific, transient noise sources (TLSs) that limit coherence in solid-state quantum hardware, which is crucial for building reliable quantum processors.
